questions.question: Length of a rectangle is 58 meters, while its breadth is 30 meters. What is the total cost of covering it with grass bed if cost is Rs. 20 per m²?

questions.question: After selling the article for Rs. 430, a person had a loss of 14%. For earning a gain of 14% how much amount an article will be sold?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price at 14% loss = Rs. 430

Desired profit = 14%

**Concept:**

⇒ Cost Price = Selling price/(1 - loss %/100)

⇒ New Selling Price = Cost Price × (1 + profit %/100)

**Solution:**

⇒ Cost Price = Rs. 430/(1 - 14/100) = Rs. 500

⇒ New Selling Price = Rs. 500 × (1 + 14/100) = Rs. 570

**Therefore, to earn a gain of 14%, the article should be sold for Rs. 570.**

questions.question: A man can swim at a speed of 14 km/hr in still water. If he takes twice the time as long to swim opposite the flow of the river than with the flow of the river, find the rate of the stream.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed in still water = 14 km/hr

Time taken to swim against the stream = 2 × Time taken with the stream

**Concept:**

The speed of the stream can be found with the relation: Speed of man in still water = ½(Speed with the stream + Speed against the stream)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Speed with the stream = 14 + s (where s = speed of the stream)

⇒ Speed against the stream = 14 - s

⇒ Time with the stream = Distance/(14 + s)

⇒ Time against the stream = Distance/(14 - s)

Considering, Time against the stream = 2 × Time with the stream:

⇒ Distance/(14 - s) = 2 × (Distance/(14 + s))

Solve the equation to find the value of 's'.

The distance cancels out: 1/(14 - s) = 2/(14 + s)

Cross multiplying and simplifying gives: 28 - 2s = 14 + s ⇒ s = 14/3

**Therefore, the rate of the stream is approximately 14/3 km/hr.**

questions.question: In the situation of liquidity trap, the speculative money demand function becomes __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**infinitely elastic**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A liquidity trap** occurs when interest rates are so low that monetary policy becomes ineffective in stimulating economic growth.
 
• In such a situation, the speculative money demand function becomes** infinitely elastic** because people prefer to hold cash rather than invest in assets that offer low returns.
 
• This means that even if the central bank increases the money supply, it will not lead to an increase in investment or consumption because people will simply hoard the extra cash.
 
• Therefore, fiscal policy, such as government spending or tax cuts, may be more effective in boosting demand and stimulating economic activity.
 
• Option 1, unitary elastic, is incorrect because it implies that a small change in interest rates would lead to an equal change in the demand for money. This is not the case in a liquidity trap where people are indifferent to changes in interest rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Inelastic money demand function means that people are willing to hold a fixed amount of money regardless of changes in interest rates or income levels.
 
• Zero money demand function means that people do not want to hold any money and prefer to invest all their wealth in other assets. This is an extreme case and not relevant in practice.
 
• Infinitely elastic money demand function means that people are willing to hold any amount of money at a given interest rate. This is the case in a liquidity trap where people are willing to hold cash even at zero interest rates.
